title: Mother's Maiden Name (Again)
summary: Chapter One, session one. Six volunteers -- any age, any background, all new to the city -- travel in separately, then are processed into civil defence together over one ordinary day: a medical, a kit issue, an errand into the city, a canteen, and a night shift clearing vermin out of a storm drain. Nothing that happens to them today is dangerous, and two things that happen to them today are the whole campaign.
structure: Four quarters, many short scenes rather than four long ones. The morning and noon are warm and administrative, the afternoon takes them into the city and introduces the most important stranger they will ever meet, the evening is the table falling in love with an NPC, and the night is a completely routine SF2E first combat that will matter more than anyone at the table can currently tell.
designRequirement: Make the players like each other's characters before anything is at stake. Plant the DNA flag. Put the antagonist in front of them and make them like him. Do not explain the Frames, the Watcher, Cicada, the mitflits or the Gap.
castingNote: Make the table love Taka tonight. Everything he is for later depends on it.
downtime: None. One continuous day of intake — the four-slice economy is taught next session, when there is something worth spending a slice on.

scenes.title: The Road In
scenes.description: The same acceptance letter, six separate journeys. A montage: each player says how their own character gets here and who they were the day before. Deliberately no shared beat -- they do not meet yet.

scenes.title: Intake Medicals
scenes.description: A queue, a form that asks for mother's maiden name twice, and a two-hundred-year-old doctor telling each of them privately that their blood screen came back irregular and not to worry about it. This is where the six of them are a group for the first time.

scenes.title: Kit Issue
scenes.description: A busy quartermaster's counter. Every player picks personnel equipment from a curated Directorate menu, and every player gets one small, unexplained extra from Nobu -- a plant, not a payoff, for much later. Personnel kit only: vehicles and Frames are Session Two's business, and the ground-role pick was removed from this scene 2026-09-13 so the players make one set of decisions tonight rather than two. GM tool: @UUID[Macro.865e0ce3b7d302e5]{Open Equipment Locker} -- opens the real inventory UI, already showing every connected player the same catalogue and budget.

scenes.title: The Errand
scenes.description: A collection run into the city -- the session's only exterior, and the only time all six are outdoors together. The Directorate's docket lists the item under a catalogue name nobody has used in a century, so the task is unfinishable until a retired chemist in a tea house reads it in nine seconds and explains it twice because he enjoys explaining. He is kind, he is useful, he says one true and unsettling thing about their employer, and he offers them a way to reach him again. GM-ONLY: he is the campaign's primary antagonist and nothing in the scene may suggest it.

scenes.title: Canteen
scenes.description: Taka renames all six of them before the plates are cleared, and the wider trainee body gets its first real screen time. Ends cold: a tannoy reads Section Nine's assignment last, worst, and non-negotiable -- storm drain clearance. Whether the party knows it's more than that depends on what they asked.

scenes.title: Flood Tunnel Clearance
scenes.description: The campaign's first fight. Two quick checks to get the drainage/compactor system running, which is what wakes the six Giant Centipedes nesting in it. An optional 'closing in' hazard (the compactor cycle itself) can run alongside the fight for a harder, more tactical version. Ends with a long rest back at student accommodation, and the six of them realising, over the water, that they were all flagged.

requiredBeats: Every one of the six is told privately that their screen flagged, and the party works out it was all of them.
Nobody explains what the screen tests for. Shucks is forbidden, and he thinks the rule is stupid.

An old man in a tea house solves a problem the Directorate could not, says one true thing about the Directorate, and leaves the party a way to contact him. Nothing in the scene suggests he is anything other than kind, because in that scene he is nothing other than kind.
danglingThreads: What a blood screen with a pre-printed IRREGULAR tick-box is actually looking for.
What the blacked-out paragraph in the founding charter says, and who painted over it.
Who the old man in the tea house is, and why a retired chemist reads a two-century-old catalogue like sheet music.
That trainee messages are read as routine policy, and that the party agreed to it this morning without reading the form.
notes: The Road In, Intake Medicals, Kit Issue and Canteen are authored. The remaining quarter — the flood tunnel clearance (now six Giant Centipedes, not mitflits — see ideas/story/bible/species/mitflits.md) — is outlined in ideas/story/blank-inheritance-ch1-v2.md and not yet written as a brief.
